title: Regional tiling and KV churn - capacity estimates
content:
Purpose:
Estimate incremental GPU memory and cluster capacity impact from onboarding the new tiled-quant model v2 with regional tiling + expected KV churn profile. Focus: per-region warmup spikes, steady-state KV footprint per shard, and recommended staging to avoid cross-region saturation.

Executive summary:
- Baseline: current fleet steady-state global KV resident = 18 TB across 240 shards (avg 75 GB/shard).
- New model v2 increases per-request KV bytes due to longer contexts and tiled prefix expansion. We estimate a +28% steady-state KV resident increase if fully rolled out without mitigations.
- Warmup (onboard) churn produces transient pressure: a 48-hour seeded warmup in a region can spike active KV occupancy by +120% above steady-state for first 36 hours.
- Recommended rollout: staged regional tiling (20% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with seeded warmup + aggressive prefix eviction policy cuts peak GPU memory demand by ~35% vs naive rollout.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Average tokens per request (post-tiling): 1,100 tokens (was 820).
- Average user session fanout: 1.2 concurrent requests per session - tiled requests create 1.6x KV entries per request on average.
- KV entry storage: 48 bytes per token (compressed + metadata) on GPU resident caches.
- Default shard size target: 64 GB usable per shard (accounting for co-host overhead).
- Warmup pattern: linear ramp of active users over 12 hours, then heavy churn for next 24 hours, decaying to steady-state by 72 hours.

Summary table (per-region estimates):
Region | Active QPS (peak) | Est. steady KV per-region (GB) | Warmup peak multiplier | Warmup peak KV (GB) | Estimated extra GPUs needed (on top of baseline) | Notes
us-west | 7,500 | 1,120 | 2.1x | 2,352 | 8 | high client concentration, consider seeded warmup
us-east | 9,800 | 1,470 | 1.9x | 2,793 | 10 | primary rollout target, high throughput
eu-west | 5,200 | 780 | 2.4x | 1,872 | 6 | higher latency profiles, tile overlap greater
apac-sg | 2,300 | 345 | 2.6x | 897 | 3 | lower baseline fleet, schedule later
sa-sao | 900 | 135 | 2.0x | 270 | 1 | optional phase 3

Calculation notes:
- Est. steady KV per-region (GB) = Active QPS * avg_seq_len * bytes_per_token * working_set_multiplier * warm_fraction_factor / 1e9.
- Warmup peak = steady * warmup_multiplier (measured from historical tiled-model rollouts where new tiling created prefix duplication).
- Estimated extra GPUs = ceil((warmup_peak_GB - baseline_region_reserve_GB) / gpu_mem_per_node_GB). We assume 300 GB usable GPU memory per node for allocation to KV caching after runtime and model weights.

Sensitivity analysis (short):
1) KV compression improvement -10% (bytes_per_token from 48 -> 43): reduces steady-state resident by ~6% and peak by ~5.5%.
2) Higher churn (1.4x fanout) increases steady-state KV by ~18% and makes warmup spikes ~1.2x larger -> require +2-3 GPUs in top regions.
3) Staggered tiling window (8h shifts across regions) lowers global simultaneous warmup overlap; reduces global peak GPU add by ~40% vs full simultaneous rollout.

Mitigations and operational levers (with rough impact estimates):
- Seeded warmup (recommended): Pre-populate hot prefixes for 7–14 days using synthetic traffic; reduces first-48h peak by 45-60%.
- Prefix eviction policy tuning: Move from LRU-ttl 14d to LRU-weighted-by-access to keep GPU resident set < target; ~20% steady mem savings in mid-tail-heavy regions.
- Regional tiling throttles: Per-route rollout pct gating (20/50/100) with automated backpressure if cache miss ratio > 8% during stage -> prevents cascading evictions.
- Compression A/B test: Deploy experiment with quantized KV packing to 10% of traffic; if CPU overhead < 12ms p99, roll to 50%. Potential 5–12% memory save.

Operational runbook (short):
- T-minus 14 days: start seeded warmup job to pre-populate top-50 prefixes in us-east and us-west. Monitor resident set and miss ratio daily.
- T-minus 7 days: enable regional tiling feature flag in canary infra regions with PR 542.
- Rollout day 0-2 (us-east): 20% traffic for 24h, evaluate miss ratio, eviction churn, and per-GPU memory headroom; if stable, move to 50% for 24h, then 100%.
- Post-rollover (72h): run KV compaction and promote hotspots to long-lived tier if access > 0.6 over 24h.

Risks and unknowns:
- Model v2 changes to tokenization may increase effective bytes_per_token; need validation with sample production traffic in canary.
- Cross-region client affinity unknown for some enterprise customers; skewed affinity could make some regions hotter than projections.
- Co-hosting with other models (edge cases) may reduce usable GPU KV capacity; plan conservative 15% cohost reserve per shard.

Action items (owners):
- Asha (infra): finalize seeded warmup scripts and schedule (due 2026-11-05).
- Jun (SRE): prepare autoscale policy that triggers early at 75% KV occupancy and test failover to secondary region.
- Diego (Applied ML): run a 48h synthetic tiling replay on staging to validate bytes_per_token and warmup multiplier assumptions.
- Maya (Console): add per-route KV-resident telemetry panels and a rollout gating dashboard (JIRA INF-7890).

Appendix - small worked example (us-east):
- Active QPS 9,800 * avg_seq 1,100 tokens = 10.78M tokens/s in-flight.
- bytes_per_token 48 -> 517.44 MB/s of KV growth sustained; with a working_set_fraction 0.25 (hot prefixes) create ~1,470 GB steady resident.
- Warmup multiplier 1.9 -> 2,793 GB peak; with 300 GB per GPU usable -> ~9.3 GPUs -> round up to 10 GPUs extra for safe headroom.

Notes for follow-up: capture real canary telemetry for bytes_per_token and warmup multiplier after first 24h of regional seeded warmup. Update this sheet with measured metrics and iterate on eviction thresholds.
